subject: social
topic: Micro-influencers trigger higher levels of trust than traditional celebrity endorsements
angle: While parasocial relationships and similarity are linked to product interest, a higher follower count is linked to increased trustworthiness and purchase intention, and indirect sources can sometimes be perceived as more credible than direct ones.
title: The Architecture of Trust

hooks.text: Why do you trust the crowd more than the person?
You think similarity builds trust. Scale actually does.
You are letting follower counts dictate your beliefs.
A screen glows in a dark room.

reveal.headline: High follower counts increase perceived trustworthiness.
reveal.body: A larger number of followers is linked to higher source trustworthiness and purchase intention.

explain.headline: The source of the message matters.
explain.body: Content from indirect sources can be perceived as more credible and less biased than content from the athlete directly.

matters.headline: Your trust is shaped by scale.
matters.body: That may be why you trust a large public figure more than a peer. Similarity and fairness build a connection, but scale builds the authority you accept.

example.headline: Scrolling a feed at night.
example.body: You see a product review from a massive account. You believe the claim because of the numbers behind it, not the person behind the camera.

verdict: The evidence shows that while interpersonal factors like similarity and fairness build parasocial relationships that drive interest, larger follower counts and third-party sources also play significant roles in credibility and purchase intent.
caveat: The study on parasocial relationships is an observational study showing associations rather than direct causation.
caption:
Your perception of trust is influenced by more than just personal connection.

Research shows that while similarity and fairness build parasocial relationships, larger follower counts are linked to higher trustworthiness and purchase intent. Some evidence suggests indirect sources are seen as more credible than direct ones. Note that the study on parasocial relationships shows associations rather than direct causation.
